We tried it on 2026 Polymarket questions with GLM-5.3 Flash. Trained on the live web, about 90% of training groups taught the model nothing because it could just look up the answer. With Time Machine, its held-out score went from 0.77 to 0.80, above the market's 0.79. https://t.c

This allows you to post-train agents to predict the future. Give an agent a past question, let it research the web as it was, and score it on what actually happened. When you do that at scale, you get agents that are genuinely good at prediction markets.

Basically, you need the internet frozen on a specific date. Every time we crawl a page, we keep a dated copy. Set snapshot_as_of, and search and page reads only see copies from that date or earlier. A page later updated with the answer can't leak it. https://t.co/exT0VUl50m

But you can't rigorously test predictions on the live web. It already knows what happened. Leaky setups reward models that cheat. So we need a version of the web set up to help us train models that understand.
A fundamental way to measure intelligence is the ability to predict the future. Kenneth Craik wrote about this in 1943, and Yann LeCun and Elon Musk have said versions of it since.

We're building a time machine for the internet.

Perplexity Time Machine shows a model the web exactly as it was on any date you pick. This allows you to post-train agents that can be good at predicting the future.
